stem: Who among the following issued the ‘Communal Award’?
expl: No consensus was made on the subject of separate electorate for Depressed Classes and various communities in Second Round Table Conference. The His Majesty Government's declared position (endorsed by Parliament) that if communities failed to agree the government would devise and apply a scheme. As a result British PM Ramsay MacDonald found a solution. Accordingly, Ramsay Macdonald declared his “Communal Award” on 16 Aug. 1932 A.D.

stem: A separate electoral group was made by the communal Tribunal of Ramsay MacDonald fi rst time in August, 1932–
expl: British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald announced Communal Award on 16 August 1932 A.D. According to Legislative Assembly provisions, few seats of Legislative Assembly were reserved for minorities whose candidates were to be elected by separate electorates members of the depressed classes qualifi ed to vote, will vote in a general constituency and they are also entitled to vote in a general constituency. Muslims and Sikhs were already considered minorities (although Europeans, Anglo-Indians, Indian Christians were provided with separate electorates in 1919). Now the Depressed Classes (untouchables) were to be declared minorities as per provisions of the new law.

stem: Which were not allocated separate electorates and reserved seats by Communal Award of MacDonald?
expl: British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald announced Communal Award on August 16, 1932 A.D. in which separate electorates were granted not only to Muslims but also to Depressed Classes. In addition to this Indian Christians, Sikhs, Anglo-Indians and others were granted the separate electorates which were applicable only to provincial Legislative Assemblies. Hence, it is clear that Buddhists were not granted separate electorates.

stem: How many seats were given to depressed classes under Communal Award and Poona Pact?
expl: The number of reserved seats for depressed classes in Provincial Legislatures were 71 in Communal Award which was increased to 148 by Poona Pact (Madras =30, Sindh with Bombay = 15, Punjab = 8, Bihar and Odisha = 18, Central Provinces = 20, Assam= 7, Bengal = 30, United Provinces= 20). Though, some books mention that there are 147 seats. In addition to this, 18% seats in General class seats were reserved for depressed class in Central Legislature.

expl: On 16 August, 1932 A.D., Ramsay Macdonald announced his Communal Award. The award authorised Indian Christians, Muslims, Europeans, Sikhs, Depressed Classes and others to have separate electorates. Gandhi began fast unto death on 20 September, 1932 A.D. to protest against this decision. Finally, on 24 September, 1932 A.D. an agreement was made in Poona known as ‘Poona Pact’ in which joint electorate was accepted on the basis of two provisions. The two provisions were – Firstly, there were 148 seats reserved for depressed classes in the provincial legislature while only 71 seats were reserved according to communal award. In Central Legislature 18 percent of the seats allotted to the general electorate were reserved for depressed classes. So reason (R) explains assertion (A) correctly, and both statements are true. So, the option (a) is correct answer.

stem: Which of the following did not sign on historical Poona Pact of 1932?
expl: On the day of 24 September, 1932, Poona Pact was signed at 5 O’clock in the evening. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar from depressed classes and Pt. Madan Mohan Malviya from Hindu classes signed the document of Poona Pact. M.M. Jayakar, Devdas Gandhi, Vishwas, Raja Bhoj, P. Baloo, Gavai, Thakkar, Solanki, Tej Bahadur Sapru, G. D. Birla, Rajagopalachari, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Dr. Rao Bahadur Srinivasan, M.C. Rajah, C.V. Mehta, Bakhale and Kamath were other signatories. Many people signed on the document in Bombay. Rajgopalachari changed his pen with Dr. Ambedkar after signing the Poona Pact.

stem: Who of the following said, “Mahatma Gandhi like fl eeting phantom raises dust but not the level”?
expl: On 14 August, 1931 A.D., Dr. B.R. Ambedkar said during a conversation with Gandhi in Mumbai “History tells that Mahatmas, like fl eeting phantoms, raise dust but not level.” It was noted that there was a conflict between Gandhi and Ambedkar on the matter of “situations of depressed classes.” Gandhiji began fast-unto-death on 20th September, 1932 against Communal Award of Prime Minister Ramsay Macdonald. Poona Pact was signed between the followers of Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
